status_reason: Material (powder blend with API), quantity (API concentration) and location (tablet press feed frame) are stated, so a first assessment is possible; the old calibration cannot be assumed valid and Raman does not keep it valid.
answer: The old NIR calibration cannot be reused on the new API and excipient blend without testing, and adding Raman does not preserve it, because a combined NIR+Raman model is a new model that needs its own calibration and validation. First test the NIR reflection probe at the feed frame on the new blend against independent laboratory API values. Test a combined NIR+Raman probe only if NIR alone fails on the same validation data.

inline.headline: Test NIR reflection probe at the tablet press feed frame on the new blend, against independent lab API values, before reusing the old calibration
inline.probe: NIR diffuse reflection probe for powder
inline.install: tablet press feed frame, where the existing NIR pilot already measures
inline.test_against: Raman probe at 785 nm excitation on the same feed frame
inline.not_final_because: The old model was built for the old matrix and is unvalidated for the new blend; NIR bands overlap and may not separate the new components, and the listed silica fiber range ends at 2400 nm while NIR is listed to 2500 nm.

problems.text: The old NIR calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend: NIR calibrations are chemometric models that are built and validated for one matrix, so the old model must be re-tested and most likely replaced by a new calibration.

Adding Raman does not keep the old calibration valid: a combined NIR+Raman model is built on newly fused data and needs its own calibration and validation on the new blend; whether fusion helps this blend is a hypothesis to test.
NIR is listed to 2500 nm but the silica Vis-NIR fiber range is 350-2400 nm; confirm which spectral window is used and whether the fiber covers it.
Raman signals are weak and can be masked by much stronger fluorescence from many organic compounds; check whether the new API and excipients fluoresce before relying on Raman.

methods.why: Most common online fiber-probe method, suited to remote probes, and already used at the feed frame; diffuse reflectance fits powder.

methods.method: Raman (785 nm excitation; Raman shift in cm-1)
methods.why: Carries information complementary to NIR on the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, but needs special probes and fluorescence can mask it.
The feed-frame study reported better API potency prediction with fused NIR+Raman, but only in that study; test it only if NIR alone fails.
Mid-IR is limited to very thin layers (usually under 50 µm) and ATR suits liquids, pastes and soft solids, not a dense powder feed.

questions.q: What is the API concentration range and the independent laboratory reference method (with sample count) used for the old calibration?
questions.why: Reference values must come from independent lab analysis, and the new blend needs its own reference set to test the old model.

questions.q: How do the API and excipient types and proportions of the new blend differ from the old formulation?
questions.why: NIR bands overlap, so any change in excipients changes the spectrum that the model reads.

questions.q: Do you already have spectra of the new API and excipients, pure or as blends?
questions.why: Spectral features of the new components are needed to judge whether NIR sees the difference.

questions.q: Does the new blend fluoresce under 785 nm excitation in your lab?
questions.why: Strong fluorescence can mask Raman and decides whether a Raman add-on is feasible.

questions.q: What prediction error limit defines pass or fail for API potency?
questions.why: Go/no-go criteria come from the client; without them the test cannot be judged.

experiment.objective: Decide whether the old NIR calibration can be reused on the new blend, and if not, whether a new NIR model or a combined NIR+Raman model is needed.
steps: Prepare new-blend calibration and validation sets across the API concentration range, with separate samples for validation.
Analyse all reference samples by an independent laboratory method for API concentration; do not use the instrument's own calibration as reference.
Record NIR spectra with the reflection probe at the feed frame (or a bench analogue) and apply the old calibration to the new-blend spectra to measure bias and error.
If the old calibration fails, build a new NIR model on the new blend and, only if needed, a NIR+Raman model with a Raman probe at 785 nm, both evaluated on the same validation set.
Confirm the spectral window and fiber transmission (silica 350-2400 nm) and check the new blend for fluorescence.
references: De Man, A, et al. (2024). Evaluating the improvement of blend potency measurements in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press using combined NIR and Raman spectroscopy. Analytical Chemistry, 96(26), 10586-10593.
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client (prediction error limit for API potency); AFS does not set them.

pathway.key_features: Key spectral features of the new API and excipients are not identified yet; they must come from the lab test spectra before a model is chosen.
pathway.path_reason: Key spectral features are not yet identified for the new blend; the guided pathway needs the multi-method lab test first.

multispectral.why: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and asymmetric polar groups, while Raman gives the molecular backbone and symmetric non-polar groups, so the information is complementary.
multispectral.test: Build NIR-only and NIR+Raman models on the same calibration and validation sets; accept the combination only if it beats the best single method (NIR alone) on that validation data.
